options.name: access_token
options.description: An OAuth2 access token if credential type is accesstoken.

options.name: addons_config
options.description: Configurations for the various addons available to run in the cluster.

options.name: auth_kind
options.description: The type of credential used.

options.name: binary_authorization
options.description: Configuration for the BinaryAuthorization feature.

options.name: cluster_ipv4_cidr
options.description: The IP address range of the container pods in this cluster, in CIDR notation (e.g. 10.96.0.0/14). Leave blank to have one automatically chosen or specify a /14 block in 10.0.0.0/8.

options.name: database_encryption
options.description: Configuration of etcd encryption.

options.name: default_max_pods_constraint
options.description: The default constraint on the maximum number of pods that can be run simultaneously on a node in the node pool of this cluster. Only honored if cluster created with IP Alias support.

options.name: description
options.description: An optional description of this cluster.

options.name: enable_kubernetes_alpha
options.description: Kubernetes alpha features are enabled on this cluster. This includes alpha API groups (e.g. v1alpha1) and features that may not be production ready in the kubernetes version of the master and nodes.

options.name: enable_tpu
options.description: (Optional) Whether to enable Cloud TPU resources in this cluster. See the official documentation - U(https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/kubernetes-engine-setup) .

options.name: env_type
options.description: Specifies which Ansible environment you're running this module within. This should not be set unless you know what you're doing. This only alters the User Agent string for any API requests.

options.name: initial_cluster_version
options.description: The software version of the master endpoint and kubelets used in the cluster when it was first created. The version can be upgraded over time.

options.name: initial_node_count
options.description: The number of nodes to create in this cluster. You must ensure that your Compute Engine resource quota is sufficient for this number of instances. You must also have available firewall and routes quota. For requests, this field should only be used in lieu of a "nodePool" object, since this configuration (along with the "nodeConfig") will be used to create a "NodePool" object with an auto-generated name. Do not use this and a nodePool at the same time. This field has been deprecated. Please use n

options.name: ip_allocation_policy
options.description: Configuration for controlling how IPs are allocated in the cluster.

options.name: kubectl_context
options.description: The name of the context for the kubectl config file. Will default to the cluster name.

options.name: kubectl_path
options.description: The path that the kubectl config file will be written to. The file will not be created if this path is unset. Any existing file at this path will be completely overwritten. This requires the PyYaml library.

options.name: legacy_abac
options.description: Configuration for the legacy ABAC authorization mode.

options.name: location
options.description: The location where the cluster is deployed.

options.name: locations
options.description: The list of Google Compute Engine zones in which the cluster's nodes should be located.

options.name: logging_service
options.description: The logging service the cluster should use to write logs. Currently available options: logging.googleapis.com - the Google Cloud Logging service. none - no logs will be exported from the cluster. if left as an empty string,logging.googleapis.com will be used. Some valid choices include: "logging.googleapis.com", "none"

options.name: master_auth
options.description: The authentication information for accessing the master endpoint.

options.name: master_authorized_networks_config
options.description: Configuration for controlling how IPs are allocated in the cluster.

options.name: monitoring_service
options.description: The monitoring service the cluster should use to write metrics. Currently available options: monitoring.googleapis.com - the Google Cloud Monitoring service. none - no metrics will be exported from the cluster. if left as an empty string, monitoring.googleapis.com will be used. Some valid choices include: "monitoring.googleapis.com", "none"

options.name: name
options.description: The name of this cluster. The name must be unique within this project and location, and can be up to 40 characters. Must be Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Must start with a letter. Must end with a number or a letter.

options.name: network
options.description: The name of the Google Compute Engine network to which the cluster is connected. If left unspecified, the default network will be used.

options.name: network_config
options.description: Network configurations .

options.name: network_policy
options.description: Configuration options for the NetworkPolicy feature.

options.name: node_config
options.description: Parameters used in creating the cluster's nodes. For requests, this field should only be used in lieu of a "nodePool" object, since this configuration (along with the "initialNodeCount") will be used to create a "NodePool" object with an auto-generated name. Do not use this and a nodePool at the same time. For responses, this field will be populated with the node configuration of the first node pool. If unspecified, the defaults are used.

options.name: private_cluster_config
options.description: Configuration for a private cluster.

options.name: project
options.description: The Google Cloud Platform project to use.

options.name: release_channel
options.description: ReleaseChannel indicates which release channel a cluster is subscribed to. Release channels are arranged in order of risk and frequency of updates.

options.name: resource_labels
options.description: The resource labels for the cluster to use to annotate any related Google Compute Engine resources.

options.name: scopes
options.description: Array of scopes to be used

options.name: service_account_contents
options.description: The contents of a Service Account JSON file, either in a dictionary or as a JSON string that represents it.

options.name: service_account_email
options.description: An optional service account email address if machineaccount is selected and the user does not wish to use the default email.

options.name: service_account_file
options.description: The path of a Service Account JSON file if serviceaccount is selected as type.

options.name: shielded_nodes
options.description: Shielded Nodes configuration.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the given object should exist in GCP

options.name: subnetwork
options.description: The name of the Google Compute Engine subnetwork to which the cluster is connected.
